**Starts** once #71 is merged.

## Design

- [Code review design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/code-review.md), sections 3, 4.1 to 4.4, and 4.8, and the sandbox in section 4.6 (settled in #82).
- ~~[Code review evaluation](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/code-review-evaluation.md), sections 6 and 8: the corpus, and the stock review's results to compare with.~~ Dropped 2026-10-20 in chat: the reviewer isn't tested on the old corpus. It's judged on new PRs, which build a new corpus (code review design sections 4.8 and 4.9).

## Open questions

- ~~How can the workflow tell that a review ran, when all its commands were blocked? (Moved from #71.)~~ Moved to #77 on 2026-10-20. It matters most when the loop stops on a review that marked nothing "fix".
- ~~Is a design doc that doesn't match the code above the bar? Agents build from the design docs, so a wrong one leads to wrong code later. The stock review rarely finds these (research doc, section 8.3). (Moved from #71.)~~ Settled 2026-10-19 in chat: yes. A wrong design doc is F6 in the rubric in code review design section 3.1 (#79).
- ~~The corpus runs need more than round 1's script did. How is our prompt copied into each clone, which is cut at an old commit? How is the task handed in, since `gh` is blocked: the plan phase for batch 4, and the PR description as it was for PR #44? How are earlier rounds' findings handed in for PR #44 rounds 2 to 4, so the reviewer doesn't post them again? And which commit ends each PR #44 round? From the branch, they look like `8d3d3a1`, `9a68517`, `3035d77`, and `ae79839`. Check each against its CI run.~~ Dropped 2026-10-20 in chat: the reviewer isn't tested on the old corpus. It's judged on new PRs, which build a new corpus (code review design sections 4.8 and 4.9).
- ~~The deferred-work rule (agreed in chat 2026-10-20, going into section 3.1) has the reviewer read the issue a code comment hands work to. Can the "Code review" workflow read issues, and which `gh` command does it allow for that?~~ Settled 2026-10-20 in chat: give the review job `issues: read`, and the reviewer reads the issue with `gh issue view`. `gh` is already allowed, and the sandbox already lets it reach `api.github.com`. Now a Do item.
- ~~How do the fix loop and the reviewer keep track of V1 findings, the ones marked "check"? Joe suggested listing them in the PR description, but DEVELOPMENT.md section 7 keeps that to the task and the "Done when" results. Set aside on 2026-10-20 until the loop runs, to see how the signals between the agents work in practice.~~ Moved to #77 on 2026-10-20.
- ~~When a call is refused that the design doesn't refuse, and the error gives the wrong reason, is it F2 or N3? Round 4 item 33-1: `removeStops` given the same stop twice refuses the second copy with "These stops aren't on the day." The design refuses it only when a stop isn't in the itinerary. Both labelers said N3, from the new wording for an error with the wrong reason. Claude's call was F2. Set aside on 2026-10-20 as one item, not enough to change the rubric. Watch for it as the rubric is used.~~ Settled 2026-10-20 in chat: no rubric change for one item.

## Do

- Write our own review prompt, as code review design sections 4.1 to 4.4 describe.
- Label the corpus with the rubric in section 3.1: the batch 4 issues from round 1, the answer key, and PR #44's findings. Two Opus labelers each run in isolation, with only section 3.1 as the rubric, and without round 1's verdicts. A script compares them. Every disagreement, and a sample of about 20 agreements, goes to Joe. PR #44's findings check each labeler against Joe's own calls.
- Label the corpus again with the rubric as revised in #81. Two Opus labelers in fresh contexts, with only section 3.1. Joe doesn't label this run. Every disagreement goes to Joe with Claude's assessment, and Claude checks the agreements for a shared misreading. Agreed in chat on 2026-10-20.
- Label the corpus a third time, with the rubric as changed after round 2 (#81, through ca69da5). Two Opus labelers in fresh contexts, with only section 3.1. Claude reads the results by category (V, D, F, N), checks them against Joe's round 2 decisions, and gives Joe a written summary. No labeling page. The labels don't need to match Joe's on every item. Agreed in chat on 2026-10-20.
- Label again only the 34 items the F3, N3, and F7 changes touch (#81, d04db3b), to check those changes. Two Opus labelers in fresh contexts, with only section 3.1. Joe doesn't label this run. Done 2026-10-20: 7 of the 8 target items landed where the change aimed, and no item moved from a note up to a fix. The results are in `scratch/code-review-eval/labeling/round-4/`. Joe called the rubric done after this run. It gets tuned as it's used.
- ~~Write down the corpus, and where the labels live, in section 4.8.~~ Dropped 2026-10-20 in chat: the reviewer isn't tested on the old corpus. It's judged on new PRs, which build a new corpus (code review design sections 4.8 and 4.9).
- ~~Test it on the corpus, as section 4.8 says.~~ Dropped 2026-10-20 in chat: the reviewer isn't tested on the old corpus. It's judged on new PRs, which build a new corpus (code review design sections 4.8 and 4.9).
- Have the reviewer end its run with a list of the findings it didn't post: where each one is, its D label, and a sentence on why, such as which issue a D3 hands the work to. The workflow adds the list to the job summary, and saves it as `not-posted.md` in the run's artifact, so Joe can check the D labels (section 4.2). Agreed in chat on 2026-10-20.
- Switch the "Code review" workflow to it. Run it in Claude Code's sandbox with the settings in section 4.6, so its commands reach only GitHub, and let it run `node`.
- Give the review job `issues: read`, so the reviewer can read the issue a code comment hands work to, with `gh issue view` (D3 in section 3.1). Only `gh api` was tested through the sandbox (section 4.6), so check in the first run that `gh issue view` works too. Agreed in chat on 2026-10-20.

## Done when

- ~~The test results are in the PR, next to the stock review's results for the same PRs.~~ Dropped 2026-10-20 in chat: the reviewer isn't tested on the old corpus. It's judged on new PRs, which build a new corpus (code review design sections 4.8 and 4.9).
- The workflow runs our reviewer on a PR, and posts its findings marked "fix", "note", or "check".

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
